exercise.title: Busy delivery drivers
exercise.prompt:
A courier company keeps one row per delivery in the table `deliveries(driver, parcels)`.

Write a query returning the columns `driver` and `total`, where `total` is the sum of `parcels` for that driver, for drivers whose total is above 10. Order by `total` descending, then `driver` ascending.

Example: with rows ('ana', 6), ('ana', 6), ('bo', 2) the result is one row, `ana` with `12`.
exercise.referenceSolution: select driver, sum(parcels) as total from deliveries group by driver having sum(parcels) > 10 order by total desc, driver asc;
exercise.fixture:
create table deliveries (driver text, parcels integer);
insert into deliveries values ('ana', 6), ('ana', 6), ('bo', 2);
